questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: good weather, interesting culture and a high academic profile

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: golden bear orientation (that you have to pay for), a lot of important information, plus you meet locals either starting at, or transferring to berkeley.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: pretty hard, if you want to be able to pay it. I ended up staying in a room I found through Airbnb, but it was still 10k dkk a month. there are a lot of opportunities once you get there, and if I hadn't been living with a fellow danish exchange student, I would have cancelled my Airbnb and found something cheaper/closer to campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: that wherever you go, is bigger in real life, than you'd assume, from looking at a map.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: housing offered by berkeley is either crazy expensive or tiny (and shared)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: expect to change your courses within the first 2 weeks. check your courses beforehand, and sign up early. the classes get filled up quick, and then once the semester starts, people jump from class to class. you might get lucky and a spot opens up, also, talk to your fellow (exchange) students about classes they're taking.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: terribly long. given it was in the states there was a lot of processes to go through, and then University of California also has a lot stuff you need to get through, before they place you at one of the 8 (I think) campuses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: 90% of the help I got was from the other exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont know

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: go the all the different courses classes you possibly can. browse what's available, or might get available.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: as my exchange was on BA level, I wasn't allowed to pick classes with a higher number than 199 (200 and up are graduate levels, and as a BA student you can only take undergraduate classes). a lot of the classes where at a pretty elementary level, and for quite a bit of my classes I was wasting time. as exchange is on either the 5th or 6th semester, the accumulated knowledge is, in my opinion, above that of the courses offer from 1-199.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: pretty much the same, though a bit more eccentric

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
music 20 - intro to musicianship
music 31 - radical listening
music 44 - voice class
music 90 - making music

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: music 90 and music 44 (advanced class). consider music 31 if you're really into culture theory.

questions.answer: public transportation was free, in the berkeley area, as a berkeley student

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: didn't attend any. would have loved to play football or soccer, but the season is during the fall, and I was there in spring

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: recreational center, big recommendation. CAL-Day was also a lot of fun

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go out with your friends (or newly met people), say yes to activities. you'll have plenty of time for your academics throughout the semester, prioritize getting new friends in the start, as it'll get harder once the year really starts.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go on the hikes in the area, go to the city (SF). try shrooms, they're totally legal in CA, and a lot of fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: people are very open and talkative in the bay, be prepared for talking to strangers on the bus, in the supermarket, or anywhere else

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Golden bear orientation was a pretty nice way to meet locals. otherwise through clubs, sports or even the nightlife.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
read up on the courses.
meet people with openness.
enjoy yourself

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
avoid living to far south of campus. I lived right on the border to Oakland, and north Oakland can be dangerous.
aim for anything above Ashby Avenue, and you can rest easy.
emphasizing, I had a great time, but it gets sketchier the further south you go from campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting some amazing friends, both from Denmark, europe and the states.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: being very far from home for 5 months.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
